officialTitle: Tarlatamab in Small-Cell Lung Cancer after Platinum-Based Chemotherapy

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: A total of 509 patients were randomly assigned to receive tarlatamab (254 patients) or chemotherapy (255 patients).
design.notes: Prespecified interim analysis reported (data cutoff January 29, 2025). Control was investigator's choice of topotecan, lurbinectedin or amrubicin.

clinicalQuestion: Is tarlatamab superior to standard second-line chemotherapy for SCLC that progressed during or after platinum-based chemotherapy?

pico.population: SCLC progressing during or after first-line platinum-based chemotherapy
pico.outcomes: Primary: OS. Key secondary: investigator-assessed PFS, patient-reported dyspnoea and cough

arms.label: Chemotherapy
arms.regimen: Investigator's choice of topotecan, lurbinectedin or amrubicin

publications.title: Tarlatamab in Small-Cell Lung Cancer after Platinum-Based Chemotherapy.
publications.label: Prespecified interim analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: Treatment with tarlatamab resulted in significantly longer overall survival than chemotherapy (median, 13.6 months [95% confidence interval {CI}, 11.1 to not reached] vs. 8.3 months [95% CI, 7.0 to 10.2]; stratified hazard ratio for death, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.47 to 0.77; P<0.001).
Tarlatamab treatment also had a significant benefit with respect to progression-free survival and cancer-related dyspnea and cough as compared with chemotherapy.

safety.description: Adverse events of grade 3 or higher
safety.sourceQuote: The incidence of adverse events of grade 3 or higher was lower with tarlatamab than with chemotherapy (54% vs. 80%), as was the incidence of adverse events resulting in treatment discontinuation (5% vs. 12%).

safety.description: Adverse events resulting in treatment discontinuation
safety.sourceQuote: as was the incidence of adverse events resulting in treatment discontinuation (5% vs. 12%).

strengths: Randomised phase III design with OS as primary endpoint
Active, investigator's-choice chemotherapy comparator reflecting practice
Patient-reported symptom benefit in addition to survival
limitations: Patients previously treated with tarlatamab or other DLL3-directed therapy and later-line populations are not addressed by this abstract

clinicalImplications.text: Tarlatamab prolonged overall survival over standard second-line chemotherapy with less high-grade toxicity, supporting it as a preferred second-line option after platinum-based chemotherapy in SCLC.

tumourBoardPearl.text: The first randomised phase III proof that a bispecific T-cell engager beats chemotherapy in relapsed SCLC; plan for cytokine-release syndrome monitoring at initiation.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 40454646. PFS and PRO results are reported qualitatively in the abstract; values omitted. Tarlatamab dosing not printed in the abstract.
